name: file-dropped
description: Row displaying a single already-selected/uploaded file (filename + size) with download and delete actions. Plain Figma COMPONENT (no variant axis) — the designer stacked three mutually-exclusive state icons (loader-circle, check, file_filled) on top of each other inside a clipped 40x40 highlight square to document all states at once; this extractor synthesizes a `state` axis (default | uploading | done) from that stack. TODO: confirm with design whether `uploading` should animate (CSS spin) since Figma has no motion spec for it.

anatomy.notes: 925x76 row, solid 1px border (not dashed — distinguishes this from the InputFile DropZone empty state), 8px radius, 16px padding, 24px gap between icon-highlight and content. cornerRadius/padding/itemSpacing are NOT bound to Figma variables (literal values in Figma itself).

40x40 rounded square (VERTICAL auto-layout, padding 8, primaryAxisAlignItems=MAX, clipsContent=true) housing the state icon. IMPORTANT FINDING: this frame stacks all three state icons (lucide/loader-circle, 24/check, 24/file_filled) as children in that order; because the frame clips content and bottom-aligns (MAX) with only 40px of height for effectively one 24px icon + 16px padding, only the LAST child (24/file_filled) actually renders inside the visible bounds in the static Figma capture — the other two are present in the layer tree but pushed outside the clip. Isolated node screenshots of `lucide/loader-circle` (113648:1330) and `24/check` (113648:1332) both exported as empty/near-blank images, while `24/file_filled` (113648:1333) exported with visible content — this independently confirms file_filled is the resting/default state, consistent with the mapping given in the task brief. cornerRadius/padding/itemSpacing are literal (unbound).

The active state glyph. Only one of the three stacked Figma nodes is meaningfully visible per state; adapter should render a single lucide icon driven by a `state` prop rather than reproducing the stack. See variants[].layers.icon.literals.icon for the resolved lucide-react name per state, and layers.icon.color for the shared color token (all three vectors are bound to the same Figma variable, bg/brand).

TEXT node 'contract_ready_signed.pdf'. fontSize/fontFamily/fontWeight/lineHeight are literal 'Inter' 16px/400/20px — NOT bound to the Family/Label, Weight/Label, or Sizing/Text/* variables used elsewhere in the file. Flagged for designer review; not a token gap per se since nothing is bound, but it deviates from the Family/Label + Sizing/Text/Large convention seen on other Input components (e.g. dropzone-label in the sibling DropZone variant).
TEXT node '442kb'. Same literal-font caveat as filename (Inter, 16px/400, lineHeight 100%).
Button instance, Type=Tertiary/Size=Icon/State=Rest, wraps a 'Main Icon' > 'Icon/Download' instance.

Button instance, Type=Tertiary/Size=Icon/State=Rest, wraps a 'Main Icon' > 'Icon/Trash-2' instance. Its vector uses bd/danger-emphasis (not a Button-default color) — the icon itself is recolored red inside an otherwise-tertiary button.

literals.animation: spin (no explicit Figma motion spec — this node was clipped/hidden in the static capture, synthesized per task brief)

a11y.notes: Root should be a labelled group (aria-label referencing the filename) so screen readers announce the file being described before the two action buttons. Download/delete buttons need discernible accessible names (e.g. 'Download contract_ready_signed.pdf', 'Delete contract_ready_signed.pdf') since they are icon-only Buttons.
